| [CASE-307](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-307.md) | The record's history from 2026-10-07 to 2026-11-22, counted at matched age, shows claims with inbound rests_on or grounds edges taking substantive revisions about 1.45 times as often as claims with none, and the fall in revision rate over an entry's life tracking its age, not its edges | [LEAD-199](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-199.md)'s count, as it specified. Population: the 859 claim files on staging, followed through renames and formerly: fields, over the record's whole history (2026-10-07 to 2026-11-22, about 46 days). A revision is substantive if it changes the title, role, warrant, defeated_if or the body outside dated notes, after normalising away link markup, directives, cited codes and citation-only parentheses; schema backfills and bot commits are excluded. Exposure: the replayed count of other entries naming the claim in rests_on or grounds. Result, at matched age (Mantel-Haenszel by age bin): claims with any inbound edge are revised 1.47 times as often as claims with none (95% interval 1.22 to 1.77; 1.45 stratified by age and calendar week; 1.62 by risk-set matching over seven days), and title and status changes rise too. The raw fall from before to after the first edge (ratio 0.58) is the filing-day burst: it vanishes when each claim's first day is dropped (1.04). The 6+ group has 4 to 7 events and an interval including 1. Classifier precision by hand-check: about 0.7 by intent, 0.9 by the letter. 148 of the 303 revisions after a first edge fall within a day of it, so edges and revisions come in the same working sessions. | Proposed |
| [CASE-318](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-318.md) | A pilot of the curation-completeness study on four replayed single-work readings: a replay from the source and the record as it stood recovers about two-thirds of what each filing held and none of what later corrections added | A pilot of [CASE-251](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-251.md)'s design, for [LEAD-014](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-014.md). Four past readings of arXiv works that a later commit corrected were chosen by a rule written first: the parameter-space symmetry survey ([LIT-970](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-970.md)), Mehta and Schwab ([LIT-882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-882.md)), Wang et al. on ambiguous phrases ([LIT-842](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-842.md)) and Lubana et al. ([LIT-669](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-669.md)). For each, an accounting was written from the source and a checkout of the record at the filing's parent commit, under the read-and-file skill's accounting step and a codebook fixed beforehand, then scored item by item. Pooled, the replays recovered 95 of the 138 items the filings held (0.69; per filing 0.61 to 0.75) and none of the 6 items the corrections added. Five of those six needed a work other than the source; the sixth was in an appendix the replay did not read. The replays also found items neither held, among them an error in Wang et al. that [NOTE-645](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-645.md) still repeats. The replays were done and scored by one assistant instance, not by separate agents, and that instance, its scoring and the original filers are one model family; no exchange was eligible, because none is held in the repository. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
